bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cm4g13.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portuguese FA provisionally suspend forward after leaving international camp
bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cm4g13.author: Paul Battison

paragraphs.text: The 41-year-old captain walked out of Portugal's Nations League squad in September after being an unused substitute against Norway and then finding out he would not start against Denmark.
In a lengthy statement, the Al-Nassr forward later explained he left because Portugal coach Jorge Jesus twice "broke his word", accusing him of an "absolute breach of trust".
In a statement, the FPF said a "provisional suspension" was issued on 9 October and they had marked the case as "urgent".
The FPF's rules state any player who fails to appear or walks out on international duties faces a ban of one to six months, as well as a fine.
Pedro Proenc, president of the FPF, told Portuguese outlet Record:, external "This is a time for calm and composure. We are all sitting down together at the table.
"There is a strong desire to have our captain back with us. There will be a normal disciplinary process."
Ronaldo accepted accountability and apologised to his team-mates and fans for his actions, before adding he deserved to be punished.
The five-time Ballon d'Or winner also confirmed he would not be retiring from international football as he continues to chase down 1000 career goals.
Ronaldo has scored 146 goals in 234 Portugal appearances - both men's world records - helping them win Euro 2016 and the Nations League twice.
He considered retiring from international football after the World Cup in the summer but opted to continue.
Ronaldo returned to action last week, scoring his 980th career goal in a 3-0 win for Al-Nassr over Diriyah Club.
The Ronaldo saga & how we got here
The Ronaldo saga has been rumbling on for some time, with many fans critical of former Portugal boss Roberto Martinez's insistence on starting Ronaldo at this summer's World Cup.

Things came to a head on 4 October when Ronaldo was an unused substitute in the Nations League win over Norway. The player subsequently left camp after finding out he would also not start against Denmark in November.
Ronaldo then published a near 2,000-word statement on Instagram slamming Jesus.
He apologised to fans and team-mates while dismissing any suggestion that he had played his last match for Portugal.
"We will have one or more farewell matches, there will be time for that," the statement said.
Manager Jesus had said the door remains open for Ronaldo to return if he chooses to, but has not commented on his latest statement.

Portuguese football journalist Jose Manuel Delgado told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I don't think there is a way back. In the statement, Ronaldo says he will return to the national team but at the same time he calls Jesus a liar three times.
"In the polls in Portugal, only 15% of the Portuguese were on Ronaldo's side and people think we owe him a lot but his time is already done and he must understand it.
"The problem is that Ronaldo does not understand it, he wants to keep playing as if he was 24, not 41.
"Things will never be the same again. No matter what happens, no matter if he plays again or if you have a game to say goodbye to Ronaldo things will never be the same.
"What Ronaldo did for Portuguese football is unique and incredible and we must thank him for all the service he gave to Portugal. But at 41, he has no place in the best XI of Portugal."

cbssports.com/nhl/news/rangers-igor-shes.headline: Rangers lose star goaltender Igor Shesterkin for season with lower-body injury; what's next for New York?
cbssports.com/nhl/news/rangers-igor-shes.author: Austin Nivison

paragraphs.text: Oct 10, 2026 at 1:46 pm ET • 2 min read
New York Rangers goaltender Igor Shesterkin will miss the remainder of the season with a lower-body injury, the team announced on Saturday.

Shesterkin suffered an apparent leg injury in the Rangers' loss to the Washington Capitals on Friday night as his right leg slid awkwardly into the post while scrambling to get back in position. Shesterkin fell to the ice immediately, and he needed assistance to get down the tunnel.

Prior to that loss, the Rangers were off to a terrific 4-1-0 start, and Shesterkin was a driving force behind that success. In just five appearances, Shesterkin posted 3.90 goals saved above average with a .900 high-danger save percentage, according to Natural Stat Trick.

The 2022 Vezina Trophy winner, Shesterkin has put up sparkling numbers since he entered the NHL in 2019-20. In 330 games, Shesterkin boasts a .917 save percentage, a 2.51 GAA and 22 shutouts. Over the last three full seasons from 2023-26, Shesterkin ranked third in goals saved above average with 45.4. Only Connor Hellebuyck and Andrei Vasilevskiy were better in that category.

Shesterkin was a big reason why the Rangers felt they could bounce back from a disappointing 2025-26 season, and losing the star goaltender puts a huge dent in the team's playoff hopes. It doesn't help that backup goalie Joonas Korpisalo is also hurt.

Dylan Garand replaced Shesterkin on Friday night, and Spencer Martin will be recalled from the AHL after recovering from his own injury. With the Rangers playing well early, it wouldn't be a shock to see them explore better replacement options for Shesterkin.
Where do the Rangers turn in goal?

New York won't be able to replace Shesterkin's impact because he's one of the five best goalies in the world. However, the team should be able to upgrade its current goaltending situation, which is a fairly low bar to clear.

First, there are unsigned veterans still on the open market in Petr Mrazek and James Reimer. Neither one was great last season -- hence their availability at the moment -- Reimer and Mrazek could provide a level of stability in the crease that the Rangers simply don't have right now.

New York could also explore trade possibilities, and Minnesota Wild netminder Filip Gustavsson could be a solution there. Jesper Wallstedt is the future of the crease in Minnesota, making Gustavsson more of a luxury. Would the Wild send Gustavsson to New York in exchange for some draft capital it could use to acquire a center?

The one snag in a potential Gustavsson deal is his contract. Gustavsson is in the first year of a deal that pays him $6.8 million over the next five seasons. That's a big commitment for a player who will become a backup when Shesterkin returns.

Obviously, Connor Hellebuyck has been on the trade market for months now, but that trade wouldn't make sense for the Rangers. Hellebuyck is on an expensive long-term deal, and New York would have $20 million tied up in goalies if they made that move, not to mention the astronomical acquisition cost.

However, if you'll allow me to get creative here, it's no secret that the Florida Panthers have pursed Hellebuyck. What if the Panthers traded Jacob Markstrom -- just acquired in the offseason -- to the Rangers in order to make room for Hellebuyck?

Markstrom does have a 20-team no-trade list, so the question is whether New York would be one of his 11 approved teams. Florida flipping Markstrom so quickly seems like a long shot, but the team has taken plenty of big swings in recent history.

aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/10/christa-pi.headline: Christa Pike discharged from hospital and returned to Tennessee prison
aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/10/christa-pi.author: Al Jazeera Staff

paragraphs.text: Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital and returned to a Tennessee women’s prison after surviving the US state’s attempt to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyers said on Saturday.

The 50-year-old is back in the Deborah K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center where she had been incarcerated for 30 years. She had been in hospital since September 30 when officials administered two doses of pentobarbital in an attempt to execute her.
Recommended Stories
Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing of her classmate, Colleen Slemmer.
Her lawyers said she was continuing to receive medical care in prison and that they would monitor her recovery. They also expressed gratitude to the first responders and medical team who treated her.

The failed execution has drawn attention to the US death penalty as a separate controversy unfolds over the military’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan. The former army psychiatrist was convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009. His execution is scheduled for December 3.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s announcement on Thursday of the livestream drew criticism, even from some supporters of capital punishment. Vice President JD Vance questioned on Friday whether it would happen and said he would not watch. In a social media post, Republican Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina called the proposal “beyond disgusting”.
Archbishop Paul S Coakley, president of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops, also condemned the plan, calling it “a barbaric promotion of a culture of death”.

In Tennessee, however, Pike’s failed execution has not prompted Republican legislators to reconsider capital punishment. Instead, some have discussed alternative methods, including the electric chair and firing squads.
Support for the death penalty in the US has declined from its peak in the 1990s. Ten states have abolished capital punishment since Pike was sentenced in 1996, but executions continue nationwide.
Thirty people have been executed in the US this year, with eight more scheduled, mostly in Texas and Florida.

A Pew Research Center poll in July found that about two-thirds of US adults considered the death penalty morally justified for people convicted of murder. But roughly six in 10 said it did not deter crime, while about seven in 10 said there was some risk of an innocent person being executed.

sports.yahoo.com/articles/fsu-lowest-per.headline: FSU’s lowest performers from Friday night’s loss, per PFF

paragraphs.text: A lopsided loss usually leaves plenty of blame to go around, and Florida State’s 44-20 defeat at Louisville was no exception. The Seminoles allowed the game to get away from them after building an early two-touchdown lead, with the defense struggling to contain Louisville once the Cardinals found their rhythm.

The final score told the broader story, but Pro Football Focus’ individual grades offered a more specific look at where the performance broke down. Here are Florida State’s five lowest-graded players from the loss to Louisville, according to PFF.
5. Deamontae Diggs (EDGE): 52.3
Diggs rounded out the bottom five with a 52.3 overall grade across 19 snaps. His 61.0 pass-rush grade was his strongest category, while PFF graded him at 50.5 against the run and 28.3 as a tackler.
4. Ma’khi Jones (DB): 50.2

Unlike the two players above him, Jones had a substantial role, playing 49 defensive snaps. His 65.6 run-defense grade was a positive, but a 27.0 tackling grade and 44.5 coverage grade pulled down his overall evaluation.
3. Ricky Knight III (DB): 45.4
Knight also saw limited action, appearing for five defensive snaps. He finished with a 45.4 overall grade, while PFF assigned him a 47.6 run-defense grade and 20.4 tackling mark.
2. Antonio Cromartie Jr. (S): 44.5
Cromartie’s evaluation came from an extremely limited sample, with the safety playing only two defensive snaps. His 44.5 overall grade included a 52.0 run-defense mark and a 20.4 tackling grade.
1. Jalen Anderson (EDGE): 40.8
Anderson received FSU’s lowest overall grade after playing 15 defensive snaps. PFF gave him a 47.5 run-defense grade, 46.5 tackling grade, and 46.7 pass-rush grade.

washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/10/t.headline: Trump says he will ‘make a decision’ on Hegseth plan to live-stream execution
washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/10/t.author: Dan Diamond, Katherine Doyle

paragraphs.text: President Donald Trump on Saturday said he would decide whether to live-stream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Malik Hasan, two days after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said it would be publicly shown.
“There are two thoughts: don’t show it, and show it,” Trump said at the White House. “By showing it, maybe other people won’t be doing what he did. I’ll make a decision, ultimately.”

The Pentagon said Thursday that the execution by firing squad would be live-streamed for the public to watch. It would be the first time the U.S. military broadcasts an execution live on the internet. The execution is scheduled for Dec. 3.

Faith leaders, human rights advocates and other groups criticized the announcement. Hasan, a former U.S. Army psychiatrist, in 2009 shot dozens of people at the Soldier Readiness Processing Center in Fort Hood, Texas.

“In no way can Hasan’s actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered,” Oklahoma City Archbishop Paul Coakley, the head of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops, said in a statement.
Vice President JD Vance on Friday said that he would not personally watch the live stream and suggested that the execution might not be broadcast.
Trump earlier this week approved Hasan’s death by firing squad. It would be the first U.S. military execution since 1961, according to the nonprofit Death Penalty Information Center.
The president on Friday appeared to say that he had approved Hasan’s live-streamed execution before suggesting Saturday he could change his mind.
“He was vicious, he was violent,” Trump said, adding that he was weighing different perspectives. “I know what the military would like to do.”
